drivingQuestion: Is an animal still twitching after a valid slaughter treated as already dead or as still alive?
outcomeNote: Ḥizkiyya's answer stands once R' Zeira explains it; R' Elazar rules like R' Yoḥanan on limbs, backed by Rav Oshaya's baraita; and Abaye resolves R' Zeira's dilemma stringently in both directions.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי: שׁוֹנִין יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּטְמֵאָה, וְגוֹי בִּטְהוֹרָה – צְרִיכִין מַחְשָׁבָה וְהֶכְשֵׁר מַיִם מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר.
segments.en: «Rabbi Asi says:» Some Sages «teach» that when «a Jew» slaughters «a non-kosher» animal «or a gentile» slaughters «a kosher» animal, in order for it to be susceptible to impurity of food, it is «necessary» that the «intention» of the one performing the slaughter be that the flesh be designated as food while it is still twitching. «And» furthermore, in order for the animal to be «rendered susceptible» to impurity, it requires contact with «water» or another liquid that renders food susceptible to impurity that comes «from another place.» The blood of this slaughter is not considered a liquid that renders food susceptible to impurity because it flowed from a valid slaughter.

segments.he: הֶכְשֵׁר לְמָה לִי? סוֹפוֹ לְטַמֵּא טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה, וְכֹל שֶׁסּוֹפוֹ לְטַמֵּא טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה – לָא בָּעֵי הֶכְשֵׁר.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Why do I» need the animal to come in contact with liquid in order for it to be «rendered susceptible» to impurity of food? The flesh of the animal «will eventually become impure» with a more «severe» level of «impurity» when it dies, i.e., impurity of an animal carcass. «And any» food «that will eventually become impure» with a more «severe» level of «impurity does not require» contact with liquid to be «rendered susceptible» to impurity of food.

segments.he: דְּתָנֵי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: ״וְכִי יֻתַּן מַיִם עַל זֶרַע״, מָה זְרָעִים שֶׁאֵין סוֹפָן לְטַמֵּא טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה צְרִיכִין הֶכְשֵׁר, אַף כֹּל שֶׁאֵין סוֹפוֹ לְטַמֵּא טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה צָרִיךְ הֶכְשֵׁר.
segments.en: The Gemara now explains the source of this principle. «As the school of Rabbi Yishmael teaches:» With regard to rendering food susceptible to impurity through contact with liquid, the verse states: «“But if water is put upon the seed,» and any of the carcass falls on it, it is impure for you” (Leviticus 11:38). «Just as seeds, which will never contract» a more «severe» level of «impurity,» because no form of severe impurity applies to foods other than meat, «require» contact with liquid to «render» them «susceptible» to their less severe level of impurity, «so too any» food «that will never contract» a more «severe» level of «impurity requires» contact with liquid to be «rendered susceptible» to impurity of food. By contrast, any food that will become impure with a more severe level of impurity does not require contact with liquid to be rendered susceptible to impurity of food.

segments.he: וְתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ נִבְלַת עוֹף טָהוֹר צְרִיכָה מַחְשָׁבָה וְאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה הֶכְשֵׁר? מִפְּנֵי
segments.en: «And» similarly, «it is taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Yosei says: For what» reason «did» the Sages «say» that in order for «the carcass of a kosher bird» to become susceptible to impurity it «requires» that the «intention» of the one performing the slaughter be to designate the animal as food, «but it is not required» for the bird to be «rendered susceptible» to impurity through contact with liquid? The reason is «because»

segments.he: שֶׁסּוֹפָהּ לְטַמֵּא טוּמְאָה חֲמוּרָה!
segments.en: «eventually» the carcass of the bird «will impart» a more «severe impurity» when it is in the throat of the person who consumes it. Therefore, it is not necessary for the carcass of a kosher bird to come in contact with liquid in order for it to be susceptible to impurity.

segments.he: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: הוֹאִיל וְיָכוֹל לְגוֹרְרָהּ, וּלְהַעֲמִידָהּ עַל פָּחוֹת מִכְּזַיִת.
segments.en: «Ḥizkiyya says» in response: The reason for the opinion of the Sages stated by Rabbi Asi is «since» the slaughterer «is able to chop» the animal into small pieces «and» thereby «establish» the volume of every piece of the animal «as less than an olive-bulk.» In such a scenario, the animal would not be susceptible to impurity. Therefore, it is not certain that the animal will eventually become impure with a more severe impurity.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא: וּמִי אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה הָכִי? וְהָא אִיתְּמַר: שָׁחַט בָּהּ שְׁנַיִם אוֹ רוֹב שְׁנַיִם, וַעֲדַיִין הִיא מְפַרְכֶּסֶת – חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר: אֵינָהּ לְאֵבָרִים, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: יֶשְׁנָהּ לְאֵבָרִים.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira: And did Ḥizkiyya» actually «say such» a statement? «But wasn’t it stated:» If one «slaughtered» a non-kosher animal in a valid manner by cutting the «two» simanim, i.e., the windpipe and the gullet, «or the majority of» the «two» simanim, «and» the animal «is still twitching, Ḥizkiyya says: There is no» prohibition against eating the «limbs» from such a twitching animal. Therefore, a gentile, who is prohibited from consuming a limb from a living animal, may consume this animal. «Rabbi Yoḥanan says: There is» a prohibition against eating the «limbs» of such an animal.

segments.he: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר אֵינָהּ לְאֵבָרִים: מֵתָה הִיא. רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר יֶשְׁנָהּ לְאֵבָרִים: לָאו מֵתָה הִיא.
segments.en: The Gemara explains the opinions: «Ḥizkiyya says» that «there is no» prohibition against eating the «limbs» of such an animal, as since it was slaughtered in a valid manner «it is» considered «dead. Rabbi Yoḥanan says» that «there is» a prohibition against eating the «limbs» of such an animal, as since it is twitching «it is not» yet «dead.» Therefore, since Ḥizkiyya maintains that a twitching animal is considered dead, it should have the impurity of a carcass, contrary to the opinion of the Sages cited by Rabbi Asi, as well as the mishna.

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יָצְתָה מִכְּלַל חַיָּה, וְלִכְלַל מֵתָה לֹא בָּאת.
segments.en: Rabbi Zeira «said to» Rabbi Yirmeya in response: Ḥizkiyya maintains that such an animal has «left the category of a living» animal, «but has not entered the category of a dead» animal. Therefore, it is not prohibited for a gentile to consume such an animal, but the animal does not have the impurity of a carcass.

segments.he: גּוּפָא: שָׁחַט בָּהּ שְׁנַיִם, אוֹ רוֹב שְׁנַיִם, וַעֲדַיִין הִיא מְפַרְכֶּסֶת – חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר: אֵינָהּ לְאֵבָרִים, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: יֶשְׁנָהּ לְאֵבָרִים. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: נְקוֹט לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּיָדְךָ, דְּתָנֵי רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ.
segments.en: §The Gemara discusses «the» matter «itself» of the dispute between Ḥizkiyya and Rabbi Yoḥanan: If one «slaughtered» a non-kosher animal by cutting the «two» simanim, «or the majority of» the «two» simanim, «and» the animal «is still twitching, Ḥizkiyya says: There is no» prohibition against eating its «limbs. Rabbi Yoḥanan says: There is» a prohibition against eating its «limbs. Rabbi Elazar said: Take that» opinion «of Rabbi Yoḥanan in your hand» and accept it, «as Rav Oshaya teaches» a baraita «in accordance with his» opinion.

segments.he: דְּתָנֵי רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁשָּׁחַט בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה לְגוֹי, שָׁחַט בָּהּ שְׁנַיִם אוֹ רוֹב שְׁנַיִם, וּמְפַרְכֶּסֶת – מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין, אֲבָל לֹא טוּמְאַת נְבֵלוֹת.
segments.en: «As Rav Oshaya teaches» (Tosefta, Oholot 2:1): In the case of «a Jew who slaughtered a non-kosher animal for» the consumption of «a gentile,» if «he slaughtered» it by cutting «two» simanim «or the majority of two» simanim, «and» the animal is still «twitching,» the animal «imparts impurity of food; but» so long as it is twitching it does «not» impart «the impurity of» animal «carcasses.»

segments.he: אֵבֶר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנָּה, כְּפוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַחַי, וּבָשָׂר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנָּה, כְּבָשָׂר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַחַי, וְאָסוּר לִבְנֵי נֹחַ, וַאֲפִילּוּ לְאַחַר שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ.
segments.en: «A limb that separates from» this twitching animal is considered «like» a limb that «separates from a living» animal, and as such it imparts the impurity of a carcass. «And flesh that separates from» this twitching animal is considered «like flesh that separates from a living» animal, and as such it does not impart impurity. «And it is prohibited for the descendants of Noah» to consume the flesh that separates from this twitching animal, «and» this prohibition applies «even after its soul departs.» This ruling of Rav Oshaya is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan.

segments.he: שָׁחַט בָּהּ אֶחָד, אוֹ רוֹב אֶחָד – אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין; נְחָרָהּ – אֵין בָּהּ טוּמְאָה שֶׁל כְּלוּם.
segments.en: The Gemara cites the continuation of the Tosefta: In the case where a Jew slaughtered a non-kosher animal for a gentile’s consumption, if «he slaughtered» it by cutting only «one» siman «or the majority of one» siman, and the animal is still twitching, the animal «does not impart the impurity of food» because the slaughter was invalid. Similarly, if he did not perform a valid slaughter but rather «stabbed» the animal, the animal «has no impurity whatsoever» while it is still twitching.

segments.he: וְגוֹי שֶׁשָּׁחַט בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, וּמְפַרְכֶּסֶת – מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין, אֲבָל לֹא טוּמְאַת נְבֵלָה.
segments.en: «And» similarly, in the case of «a gentile who slaughtered a kosher animal for» the consumption of «a Jew, and» the animal «is» still «twitching,» the animal «imparts the impurity of food» because it is considered to be food, «but» so long as it is twitching it does «not» impart «the impurity of an animal carcass.»

segments.he: אֵבֶר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנָּה, כְּפוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַחַי, וּבָשָׂר הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִמֶּנָּה, כְּפוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַחַי, וְאָסוּר לִבְנֵי נֹחַ, וַאֲפִילּוּ לְאַחַר שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ.
segments.en: «A limb that separates from» this twitching animal is considered «like» a limb that «separates from a living» animal, and as such it imparts the impurity of a carcass. «And flesh that separates from» this twitching animal is considered «like» flesh that «separates from a living» animal, and as such it does not impart the impurity of food. «And it is prohibited for the descendants of Noah» to consume the flesh that separates from this twitching animal, «and» this prohibition applies «even after its soul departs.»

segments.he: שָׁחַט בָּהּ אֶחָד אוֹ רוֹב אֶחָד – אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין, נְחָרָהּ – אֵין בָּהּ טוּמְאָה שֶׁל כְּלוּם.
segments.en: If the gentile «slaughtered» the kosher animal by cutting only «one» siman «or the majority of one» siman, and the animal is still twitching, the animal «does not impart impurity of food» because the slaughter was not valid. Similarly, if he «stabbed» the animal rather than slaughtering it properly, «it has no impurity whatsoever.»

segments.he: שָׁחַט גּוֹי בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ טְרֵפָה, וּבָא יִשְׂרָאֵל וּגְמָרָהּ – כְּשֵׁרָה.
segments.en: If «a gentile» partially «slaughtered» a kosher animal «in a place that does not render» the animal «a tereifa,» i.e., unfit for consumption due to a mortal wound, e.g., he cut half of the windpipe, «and» then «a Jew came and completed» the slaughter, the animal is «fit» for consumption.

segments.he: שָׁחַט יִשְׂרָאֵל, בֵּין בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ טְרֵפָה, וּבֵין בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵין עוֹשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ טְרֵפָה, וּבָא גּוֹי וְגָמַר שְׁחִיטָתוֹ – פְּסוּלָה.
segments.en: But if «a Jew slaughtered» the animal, «either in a place that renders» the animal «a tereifa,» e.g., he cut the majority of the windpipe, «or in a place that does not render» the animal «a tereifa,» e.g., he only partially cut the windpipe, «and» then «a gentile came and completed» the slaughter, «his slaughter is not valid.»

segments.he: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיֹּאכַל מִבְּהֵמָה קוֹדֶם שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ, חוֹתֵךְ כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר מִבֵּית שְׁחִיטָתָהּ, וּמוֹלְחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה, וּמְדִיחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה, וּמַמְתִּין לַהּ עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ, וְאוֹכְלוֹ. אֶחָד גּוֹי וְאֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּתָּרִין בּוֹ.
segments.en: The baraita continues: «One who wishes to eat from» the meat of a slaughtered «animal before its soul departs may cut an olive-bulk of meat from the area of its slaughter,» the neck, «and salt it very well,» i.e., more than is normally required, «and rinse it very well» in water to remove the salt and blood, «and» then «wait until» the animal’s «soul departs, and» then «eat it. Both a gentile and a Jew are permitted to» eat «it» because the prohibition against eating a limb from a living animal is not applicable in such a case.

segments.he: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין, דְּאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אַשְׁיָין: הָרוֹצֶה שֶׁיַּבְרִיא, חוֹתֵךְ כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר מִבֵּית שְׁחִיטָה, וּמוֹלְחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה, וּמְדִיחוֹ יָפֶה יָפֶה, וּמַמְתִּין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתֵּצֵא נַפְשָׁהּ, אֶחָד גּוֹי וְאֶחָד יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּתָּרִים בּוֹ.
segments.en: The Gemara notes: This baraita «supports» the opinion of «Rav Idi bar Avin, as Rav Idi bar Avin said» that «Rav Yitzḥak bar Ashyan said: One who wants to be healthy should cut an olive-bulk of meat from the area of the slaughter, and salt it very well and rinse it very well, and» then «wait until» the animal’s «soul departs,» and then «both a gentile and a Jew are permitted to» eat «it.»

segments.he: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שָׁהָה בָּהּ, דָּרַס בָּהּ – מַהוּ?
segments.en: §It was previously taught in the baraita that if a Jew slaughtered a non-kosher animal for a gentile’s consumption, or a gentile slaughtered a kosher animal for a Jew’s consumption, that animal imparts impurity of food when it is twitching after the slaughter. With regard to that halakha, «Rabbi Elazar raises a dilemma: What is» the halakha in such a case if «one interrupted» the slaughter or «pressed» on the knife during the slaughter? Do these acts, which normally invalidate slaughter, also invalidate this slaughter, or does the slaughter in this case not have to fulfill all of the halakhic requirements of valid slaughter in order to render the slaughtered animal as food with regard to imparting the impurity of food?

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא סָבָא: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: צְרִיכָה הֶכְשֵׁר שְׁחִיטָה כִּבְהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה. הֶכְשֵׁר לְמַאי? אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יִצְחָק: בְּדִיקַת סַכִּין.
segments.en: «A certain elder» resolved this dilemma and «said to him: Rabbi Yoḥanan said as follows:» This case «requires a valid slaughter» in every detail, «just like» a Jew slaughtering «a kosher animal.» The Gemara clarifies: «To what» requirement does «valid» slaughter just like a kosher animal refer? «Rav Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said:» It is referring to the requirement of «examining the knife» before the slaughter.

segments.he: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מַהוּ שֶׁתַּצִּיל עַל הַבְּלוּעִין שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ?
segments.en: «Rabbi Zeira asked Rav Sheshet:» If a non-kosher animal slaughtered by a Jew is twitching under the same roof as a corpse, and the animal swallowed items before being slaughtered, «what is» the halakha «with regard to» those swallowed items that are inside the animal? Is the animal considered to be living and therefore «it should save» these items «that are swallowed inside it» from the impurity transmitted by the corpse to all items under the same roof? Or is the animal considered to be dead and therefore the items become impure?

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין, וּמַצֶּלֶת? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת נְבֵלוֹת, וְלֹא תַּצִּיל?
segments.en: «Rav Sheshet said to» Rabbi Zeira: Since it is established that such an animal is considered to be dead and «imparts impurity of food,» is it possible that it «saves» those items inside it from impurity? Certainly it does not. Rabbi Zeira «said to him» in response: It is also established that such an animal «does not impart impurity of carcasses and» is considered to be a living animal in that regard. How is it possible that the animal «does not save» those items inside it from impurity?

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֵינָהּ מַצֶּלֶת עַל הַבְּלוּעִים שֶׁבְּתוֹכָהּ, דְּהָא מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת אֳכָלִין, וְהָרוֹבְעָהּ חַיָּיב, דְּהָא אֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה טוּמְאַת נְבֵלָה.
segments.en: «Abaye» resolved the dilemma and «said:» It is proper to treat this case stringently. Therefore, such an animal «does not save» the items «that are swallowed inside it because it imparts impurity of food. But one who engages in bestiality with» such an animal «is liable because» the animal «does not impart impurity of a carcass» and is considered to be living in that regard.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אסי: שונין
moves.summary: R' Asi reports the Sages' ruling that a Jew slaughtering a non-kosher animal, or a gentile a kosher one, requires intention and contact with liquid from elsewhere
moves.about: the Sages' teaching that a Jew slaughtering a non-kosher animal, or a gentile a kosher one, requires intention and contact with liquid from elsewhere for susceptibility to impurity of food

moves.cueHe: הכשר למה לי?
moves.summary: why should contact with liquid be needed, when whatever will end in severe impurity needs none
moves.about: why contact with liquid should be needed at all, since flesh destined to impart severe carcass impurity never requires it

moves.cueHe: דתני דבי רבי ישמעאל
moves.summary: the school of R' Yishmael derives from 'if water is put upon the seed' that only what will never impart severe impurity needs contact with liquid
moves.about: the verse on which the school of R' Yishmael builds the rule of hekhsher

moves.cueHe: ותניא, אמר רבי יוסי
moves.summary: a baraita of R' Yosei is brought to the same effect, asking why a kosher bird's carcass needs intention but not contact with liquid
moves.about: a baraita of R' Yosei on why a kosher bird carcass needs intention but not contact with liquid

moves.cueHe: שסופה לטמא טומאה חמורה
moves.summary: R' Yosei answers his own question: because the bird carcass will eventually impart severe impurity in the throat

moves.cueHe: אמר חזקיה: הואיל ויכול לגוררה
moves.summary: Ḥizkiyya answers that the animal is not certain to reach severe impurity, since it can be chopped into pieces smaller than an olive-bulk
moves.about: why the twitching animal is not certain to end in severe impurity — the slaughterer can still chop it into pieces smaller than an olive-bulk

moves.cueHe: ומי אמר חזקיה הכי? והא איתמר
moves.summary: R' Yirmeya asks R' Zeira how Ḥizkiyya could say this, given his ruling that the twitching animal's limbs are permitted because it is dead
moves.about: whether Ḥizkiyya could really have given that answer

moves.cueHe: חזקיה אמר אינה לאברים: מתה היא
moves.summary: the Gemara spells out the reasoning of each side of the dispute, sharpening the contradiction against Ḥizkiyya
moves.about: the reasoning behind Ḥizkiyya's ruling — the validly slaughtered twitching animal counts as dead

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: יצתה מכלל חיה, ולכלל מתה לא באת
moves.summary: R' Zeira answers that for Ḥizkiyya the animal has left the category of living without entering that of dead
moves.about: Ḥizkiyya is consistent: the twitching animal has left the category of living without entering the category of dead

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי אלעזר: נקוט להא דרבי יוחנן בידך
moves.summary: R' Elazar rules that R' Yoḥanan's view is to be held, since Rav Oshaya teaches in accordance with him
moves.about: which of Ḥizkiyya and R' Yoḥanan is to be held as halakha on limbs of a twitching animal

moves.cueHe: גופא
moves.summary: the dispute of Ḥizkiyya and R' Yoḥanan, cited above in passing, is now taken up for its own sake
moves.about: returning to the dispute of Ḥizkiyya and R' Yoḥanan over limbs of a twitching animal, now for its own sake

moves.cueHe: דתני רב אושעיא
moves.summary: Rav Oshaya's baraita: the twitching animal imparts impurity of food but not of carcasses, and a limb separated from it is like one from a living animal
moves.about: Rav Oshaya's baraita on a Jew slaughtering a non-kosher animal for a gentile

moves.cueHe: הרוצה שיאכל מבהמה קודם שתצא נפשה
moves.summary: the same baraita permits cutting an olive-bulk from the site of slaughter, salting and rinsing it, and waiting until the animal dies
moves.about: the baraita's ruling on cutting an olive-bulk from the site of slaughter supports Rav Idi bar Avin's teaching

moves.cueHe: מסייע ליה לרב אידי בר אבין
moves.summary: the baraita is noted as supporting Rav Idi bar Avin in the name of Rav Yitzḥak bar Ashyan
moves.about: Rav Idi bar Avin's ruling on cutting and salting an olive-bulk from the site of slaughter

moves.cueHe: בעי רבי אלעזר: שהה בה, דרס בה – מהו?
moves.summary: R' Elazar asks whether interrupting or pressing during this slaughter invalidates it for these purposes
moves.about: whether interrupting or pressing during the slaughter invalidates it for the purpose of rendering the animal food that can contract impurity

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה ההוא סבא: הכי אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: a certain elder answers in R' Yoḥanan's name that this slaughter must be valid just like that of a kosher animal
moves.about: resolving R' Elazar's dilemma — this slaughter must be valid in every respect

moves.cueHe: הכשר למאי?
moves.summary: the Gemara asks which requirement of valid slaughter is meant
moves.about: which requirement of valid slaughter R' Yoḥanan's phrase הכשר שחיטה refers to

moves.cueHe: אמר רב שמואל בר יצחק: בדיקת סכין
moves.summary: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzḥak: it refers to examining the knife
moves.about: R' Yoḥanan's הכשר שחיטה means the requirement to examine the knife

moves.cueHe: בעא מיניה רבי זירא מרב ששת
moves.summary: R' Zeira asks Rav Sheshet whether such an animal shields items swallowed inside it from corpse impurity
moves.about: whether a twitching slaughtered animal shields items swallowed inside it from the impurity of a corpse in the same tent

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: מטמאה טומאת אוכלין, ומצלת?
moves.summary: Rav Sheshet objects that an animal imparting impurity of food is treated as dead and cannot shield
moves.about: an animal that already imparts impurity of food is treated as dead and so cannot shield what it swallowed

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: אינה מטמאה טומאת נבלות, ולא תציל?
moves.summary: R' Zeira counters that it does not impart carcass impurity and so is treated as alive
moves.about: an animal that does not impart carcass impurity is treated as living and so should shield what it swallowed

moves.cueHe: אמר אביי: אינה מצלת על הבלועים שבתוכה
moves.summary: Abaye rules stringently on both sides: it does not shield, and one who copulates with it is liable
moves.about: resolving the dilemma stringently in both directions — it does not shield, yet one who copulates with it is liable

edges.proposedPredicate: interpret.derives_by_binyan_av — «מה … אף כל …» — generalises a rule from the paradigm case the verse names to every case sharing its feature; interprets_verse only says that scripture is being expounded, infers_from reads a conclusion out of a sage's wording, and derives_by_kal_vachomer is a fortiori rather than paradigm-based
